active_design_physical_activity_and_heal.description: Adults reporting a Body Mass Index over 25. People who are overweight or obese are at increased risk for heart disease and diabetes. active_design_physical_activity_and_heal.description: The percentage of the population who live within walking distance to a park: a quarter-mile or less to entrances of smaller sites, such as sitting areas and playgrounds, and half-mile or less to entrances of larger parks. active_design_physical_activity_and_heal.description: Sidewalk area percentage. Sidewalks are important for commuting, businesses, and physical activity. More sidewalk area contributes to a safer pedestrian environment, supports vibrant business districts and can foster social interaction.

active_design_physical_activity_and_heal.longName: Walking distance to a subway station, 2018

reportTopics.heading: Injury and health
reportTopics.description: Neighborhood design can influence health both directly -- by way of immediate hazards in the environment, and indirectly, for example, by encouraging exercise.

reportTopics.heading: Neighborhood resources
reportTopics.description: Aspects of the neighborhood environment can encourage walking, bicycling and participation in other healthy physical activities.

reportTopics.heading: Neighborhood risk factors
reportTopics.description: Living in high-poverty neighborhoods or in environments that feel unsafe makes it difficult to be physically active and access resources that promote health.

reportTopics.heading: Physical activity
reportTopics.description: Walking and bicycling are healthy activities that can also be used for active transportation.

reportTopics.heading: Adult asthma
reportTopics.description: Asthma symptoms in adults 18 and over. Asthma cannot be cured, but it can be controlled.

reportTopics.heading: Child asthma
reportTopics.description: Asthma is a leading cause of emergency room visits, hospitalizations and missed school days in New York City’s poorest neighborhoods. In NYC, asthma is more common among low-income Black and Latino children.

reportTopics.heading: Health burden: fine particles (pm2.5)
reportTopics.description: PM2.5 air pollution can trigger an asthma attack or make symptoms worse. Sometimes this results in an Emergency Department (ED) visit or a hospitalization.

reportTopics.heading: Health burden: ozone (o3)
